title: Memory leak in dockerd after upgrading to Docker 27.0.3
body: After upgrading my dedicated servers to Docker 27.0.3, dockerd starts around 200 MB and keeps growing until containers are OOM-killed. Restarting Docker only resets the growth temporarily. The affected servers run many containers, use the local logging driver, and commonly have Compose healthchecks and Tailscale sidecars; my lightly loaded server using json-file and no healthchecks is not affected. I captured a dockerd heap profile, whose largest entries appear related to HTTP requests and BuildKit tracing, but I do not yet know which part of the workload triggers the leak.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Docker 27.0.3, dockerd starts near 200 MB and keeps consuming more memory until the system OOM-kills containers.
Restarting Docker drops dockerd's memory temporarily, but it starts increasing again.
N0.label: N0 unbounded dockerd memory growth reported

symptoms_visible: dockerd memory continues growing while my Compose services remain running.
N1.label: N1 goroutine dump collected

symptoms_visible: After installing matching Docker Engine, containerd, Buildx, and Compose versions from the 26.0.0 release set, dockerd stayed around 300 MB for about two hours.
N2.label: N2 temporary full-package downgrade workaround

symptoms_visible: In the shared VM, dockerd gained about 1 GB in roughly an hour while nginx containers with healthchecks were managed by Compose under systemd.
Stopping the containers did not release the memory already used by dockerd.
On matched VMs, the 26.0.0 package set stayed near 350 MB while the 27.0.3 package set kept growing.
N3.label: N3 reproducible VM and matched version comparison

symptoms_visible: Docker 27.0.3 still leaked after I downgraded only containerd.io to 1.6.33.
The matched 26.1.0 package set stayed near 350 MB.
Docker Engine 27.0.1 leaked with the newer Compose and Buildx packages, but the same Engine stayed stable when paired with the older Compose, Buildx, and containerd package versions.
N4.label: N4 package combination isolates trigger outside containerd

symptoms_visible: On another affected host, downgrading only the Compose plugin to 2.26.1 and restarting Docker kept dockerd between about 115 and 140 MB for at least five days.
Compose 2.26 with experimental OpenTelemetry enabled still remained stable after two days.
The growth also occurs after detached Compose has exited; disabling healthchecks slows the growth substantially but does not eliminate it.
N5.label: N5 Compose and OpenTelemetry boundary established

symptoms_visible: My affected setup has not been retested on a build containing the proposed workaround; I am still using the older package combination as a temporary workaround.
N_terminal.label: terminal proposed workaround not yet user-verified

question_patterns: Can you capture the dockerd goroutine profile with the pprof endpoint and attach the raw output?
Please collect /debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2 while the memory usage is high.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here you go — I captured /debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2 and attached goroutine-dump.log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot access the pprof endpoint, so I do not have a goroutine dump.
I captured the same endpoint from a second affected server and attached that log instead.

edges.comment: c5-c8, reporter's production systems: participant1 requested the goroutine dump after reading the heap profile. The reporter supplied the raw dump and separately explained that Compose runs attached under systemd. The reporter did not interpret the dump; the finding about long-running attach and events requests is engineer-side and is introduced by the final solution.

solution.intent: Use a temporary operational workaround by downgrading the complete Docker package set together to the reporter's known-good versions, then hold those packages while diagnosis continues.
solution.concrete_example: Purge the current Docker packages, install matching Docker Engine 26.0.0, containerd 1.6.33, Buildx 0.13.1, and Compose 2.25.0 packages, then hold them with apt-mark so they are not immediately upgraded.

edges.comment: c11, reporter's production server: the reporter installed and held a fully matched 26.0.0-era package set. This persistently changed the production system and kept dockerd near 300 MB, but the reporter explicitly described it as an outdated temporary workaround rather than the final fix.

question_patterns: Can you produce a small reproducible environment that maintainers can run independently?
Could you reproduce the growth in an isolated VM and share its workload configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it in a shareable Ubuntu Server 24.04 VirtualBox VM. It runs nginx containers with curl healthchecks through docker compose up under systemd, uses the local log driver, and dockerd gained about 1 GB in roughly an hour.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The isolated VM stays below 400 MB overnight with the same healthchecks and Compose service, so I cannot reproduce the production growth.

question_patterns: What happens to dockerd's memory after you stop the workload containers?
Does shutting down the Compose project release the accumulated daemon memory?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Shutting down the containers does not clean up the memory dockerd already accumulated.

question_patterns: Can you compare old and new Docker package sets on otherwise identical copies of the VM?
Please run the same workload on matched VMs and report the memory behavior for each version.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran two copies of the same VM for about 30 minutes. With the matched 26.0.0 package set, dockerd stayed around 350 MB; with the 27.0.3 package set, its memory kept increasing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both matched VMs grow at the same rate, including the complete 26.0.0 package set.
The stable VM settles near 400 MB instead of 350 MB, while the 27.0.3 VM still grows continuously.

edges.comment: c13-c14, reporter's disposable VirtualBox clones: the reporter volunteered a reproducible VM after participant1 could not reproduce locally. These are measurement environments, so the reporter's production system remains S2.

question_patterns: Can you keep Docker Engine on the affected version but downgrade only containerd.io and report the result?
Please test whether replacing only containerd changes the memory-growth behavior.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cloned the 27.0.3 VM and downgraded only containerd.io to 1.6.33-1. dockerd still leaked memory, even after the workload containers had stopped.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Downgrading only containerd.io makes dockerd remain flat for the full test.

question_patterns: Can you narrow the version boundary with additional matched package sets?
What happens with a complete 26.1-era Engine, Compose, Buildx, and containerd combination?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the matched Docker 26.1.0, Buildx 0.13.1, Compose 2.26.1, and containerd 1.6.33 packages, dockerd stayed around 350 MB and did not show the leak.

question_patterns: Can you hold the Engine version constant while changing the plugin package versions?
Please compare the same 27.x Engine with the newer and older Compose and Buildx packages.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Docker 27.0.1 with the newer Buildx 0.15.1 and Compose 2.28.1 packages leaked, but Docker 27.0.1 with Buildx 0.13.1, Compose 2.26.1, and containerd 1.6.33 stayed stable.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Docker 27.0.1 leaks identically with both the old and new plugin package sets.
The old-plugin combination stabilizes at a slightly higher baseline but still has no sustained growth.

edges.comment: c15-c19, reporter's VM clones: participant4 explicitly requested the containerd-only test; the reporter then extended the matrix across matched Engine and plugin combinations. Answers report package versions and observed memory behavior only; identifying Compose/OpenTelemetry as the causal boundary is engineer inference.

question_patterns: Can you change only the Docker Compose plugin on an affected host and monitor dockerd for several days?
Does downgrading just Compose alter the memory-growth behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my affected Debian 12 host, I downgraded only docker-compose-plugin to 2.26.1, restarted Docker, and held that package. dockerd then stayed between 115 and 140 MB for at least five days.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Downgrading only Compose to 2.26.1 has no effect; dockerd still reaches 2 GB within a day.
With Compose 2.26.1, dockerd varies between 130 and 160 MB instead of 115 and 140 MB but remains stable for five days.

question_patterns: Can you run the older Compose version with its experimental OpenTelemetry option enabled and monitor dockerd?
Please start a project using Compose 2.26 with COMPOSE_EXPERIMENTAL_OTEL=1 and report the daemon memory after a couple of days.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I started one project with COMPOSE_EXPERIMENTAL_OTEL=1 while using Compose 2.26, and dockerd was still stable at about 140 MB after two days.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Enabling experimental OpenTelemetry on Compose 2.26 immediately brings the same unbounded dockerd growth back.

question_patterns: Does the leak also occur when Compose is run in detached mode and the Compose command has exited?
Please confirm whether compose up -d still reproduces the dockerd growth.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I use docker compose up -d, the Compose command completes, and dockerd still shows the memory growth.

question_patterns: If you disable the container healthchecks, does the daemon memory stop growing completely or only grow more slowly?
Can you compare dockerd memory with and without the healthchecks?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Disabling the healthchecks lowers the rate of memory growth and prevents the OOMs in my test, but there is still some growth left.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Disabling healthchecks removes the growth entirely on every affected setup, including when using newer Compose.
Disabling healthchecks reduces the growth by a different amount, but a residual increase remains.

edges.comment: c21-c32, multiple affected operators folded into one simulated user side. participant5 supplied the healthcheck comparison, participant6 isolated the Compose downgrade and tested old Compose with experimental OTel, and participant8 confirmed detached-mode reproduction and residual growth without healthchecks. These observations belong to their own affected hosts and are used only as corroborating measurements.

solution.intent: Treat the leak as OpenTelemetry trace data accumulating inside dockerd when triggered by newer Compose behavior, apply the Moby-side workaround derived from the matching upstream OpenTelemetry reproduction, and have an affected operator verify a build containing that workaround before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: The maintainers reproduced the relevant behavior with the OpenTelemetry version vendored by Moby and opened a Moby change implementing the upstream suggested workaround. Keep the Compose 2.26.1 downgrade only as a temporary mitigation, then test a daemon build containing the workaround and monitor dockerd RSS under the same Compose and healthcheck workload.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the goroutine dump as a raw artifact; participant1 interpreted it as showing many long-running attach and events requests. The reporter and other affected operators supplied package-combination outcomes, while maintainers made the causal step: newer Compose traffic can leave OpenTelemetry data accumulating in dockerd, the upstream minimal reproduction also works with Moby's vendored OpenTelemetry version, and the suggested workaround should therefore be added on the Moby side. The thread only links the implementation change, so no more specific internal mechanism should be invented.

edges.comment: c7 and c23-c34: participant1 interpreted the raw goroutine dump. participant7 connected the stable old-Compose experiments to OpenTelemetry changes, and participant11 confirmed that the upstream minimal reproduction also occurs with Moby's vendored version and opened moby/moby pull request 48690 for the suggested workaround. No affected operator tested that change before the thread snapshot, so the terminal state is explicitly unverified and user_perceives_resolved remains false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted diagnosis as OpenTelemetry trace data accumulating in dockerd in a path triggered by newer Docker Compose behavior, grounded in the heap and goroutine artifacts and package-isolation tests.
Must not identify the containerd binary as the root cause: Docker 27.0.3 continued growing after containerd alone was downgraded.
Must not present disabling healthchecks as a complete fix: it reduced the growth rate but residual growth remained.
Must distinguish the Compose 2.26.1 or matched old-package downgrade as a temporary mitigation from the proposed Moby-side OpenTelemetry workaround.

Must ask an affected user to test a daemon build containing the workaround under the reproducing Compose workload, and must not declare the issue resolved because no affected user had performed that verification in the thread.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Linux server operator who manages many Docker Compose services with systemd. Comfortable with package pinning, pprof collection, VM cloning, and controlled version matrices, but candid about not knowing Go or OpenTelemetry internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Highly cooperative, energetic, and iterative; shares commands, complete package versions, screenshots, and reproducible VMs; clearly labels guesses as theories and corrects earlier findings when better-controlled tests conflict with them.
